name: N. MACEDONIA

flag.title: Golden Sun
flag.note: Red field, golden sun with 8 rays

lead: North Macedonia is a small Balkan country. It has one of Europe's oldest lakes. People shaped the Cyrillic alphabet here. A golden sun shines on its red flag.
geo: North Macedonia has no coast. Mountains and river valleys fill the land. Golem Korab, at 2,764 m, is the peak it shares with Albania.
In the southwest, Lake Ohrid is so clear that you can see 22 m down. Lake Prespa sits higher, at 850 m. The far south feels almost like the Mediterranean.
animals: The Balkan lynx is a very rare wild cat. Fewer than 50 remain. It is on the 5-denar coin. Brown bears, grey wolves and golden eagles live here too.
Lake Ohrid has several fish found nowhere else on Earth. The Ohrid trout has pink flesh. It is now strictly protected.
culture: The national dish is tavche gravche, baked white beans in a clay pot, eaten every Friday. Ajvar is a smoky red-pepper relish made each autumn.
Dancers in embroidered costumes do the oro chain dance at village parties. The Tikveš region has made wine for over 2,500 years.
history: Philip II and Alexander the Great built their empire here in the 4th century BC. The Roman road Via Egnatia later crossed the land. Farmers still find Roman coins in their fields.
Saint Clement founded the Ohrid Literary School in the 880s, where Cyrillic was developed. The country left Yugoslavia in 1991. A 2019 deal with Greece made 'North Macedonia' official.
wows: Lake Ohrid is up to 3 million years old.
Golem Korab is the high point of both North Macedonia and Albania.
Around 300 million people use the Cyrillic alphabet, shaped at Ohrid in the 9th century.
A lake on Saturn's moon Titan is named Ohrid Lacus.
Korab Falls drops over 130 m in spring, the country's tallest waterfall.
Tikveš winery, founded in 1885, ships 15 million bottles a year.
People still walk across Skopje's 15th-century Ottoman Stone Bridge.
